<!-- pr-reviewer: c764e273b027caaf2b773b3461952150c8348342 -->
**Not built beyond xtask, and part of this is the maintainer's decision: needs a maintainer look (no code blockers found).**

This changes how every merge batch ends (a new one-line PR per batch, a new writer of `PROCESS_VERSION`, a new body line the reviewers demand). That is a process law, so I leave the call to the maintainer rather than label it merge-ready.

**What looks good**
- The rule reads the same in AGENTS.md (bullet "Process changes bump `PROCESS_VERSION`"), PR-reviewer.md:167-172, review-prs SKILL.md:231-241, merge-ready SKILL.md:151 and :227-233, and resolve-conflicts SKILL.md:101 and :185. No place still demands a per-PR bump, and none contradicts another (all say: body `Process change: yes`, file untouched, merging session bumps once per batch and posts on #681).
- The fork sync step (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session") is unchanged and still works: it compares upstream's file with the local one. The window between the files merging and the bump merging is harmless, as the text says.
- `xtask/src/process_bump.rs`: no `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests (grep clean); `bumped` parses with `u64`, uses `checked_add`, strips a BOM, refuses empty, non-integer, `-1`, `6.2`, `62 63` and `u64::MAX`; `run` turns a missing or unreadable file into an error string. It is always old+1, so it cannot write a lower or equal number.
- A decision file (`docs/decisions/1153-...`) lists what was considered and dropped.

**Results (locally, merged with main bb7729c; the diff touches `xtask/`, so pr-test.yml refuses it)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p xtask` | 121 passed, 0 failed (includes the 3 new process_bump tests) |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` plan | only "xtask unit tests", which is the run above |
| `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None blocking. Small things the author may tidy:
1. PR-reviewer.md:169-172 and review-prs SKILL.md:235 say a PR "must NOT edit" the file; this PR edits it (62 to 63, stated in the body as the last such PR). Fine for this one PR, but say in the text that the bump PR itself (`chore(process): PROCESS_VERSION <n>`) is exempt, or a reviewer reading the rule will flag it. AGENTS.md also does not say whether that one-line PR is reviewed or merges straight away.
2. AGENTS.md:90 and resolve-conflicts SKILL.md:164 (and merge-plan's `MECHANICAL` list, `xtask/src/merge_plan.rs:12`) still call `PROCESS_VERSION` a rule-settled file. That is right for old branches (a stale edit of the file conflicts with the bump PR on that one line; `resolve-conflicts` says take main's, and `merge-plan` reads it as MECHANICAL), so I would keep it, with a half-sentence saying why.

**Questions / notes for the maintainer (the decision part)**
- No gate enforces the bump. If a merging session forgets `cargo xtask process-bump` after a batch, forks never see a higher number and never sync the new process files. Today the writer was the PR, which could not be forgotten. Worth deciding whether `merge-ready`'s "After all merges" step is enough or `merge-plan` should print a reminder when a batch had process PRs.
- One extra PR per batch with a process change goes through main's protection like any other (0 approvals, same account), so it fits; the cost is one more merge and a short wait.
- Not exercised: the bump-PR flow itself (first use is the merge of this PR) and the `#681` announcement.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 2672dcd393cc02dfa7b99018b881f7d4138e4d86 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge (delta review of c764e273..2672dcd3).

What looks good
- The new commit is wording only: PR-reviewer.md, review-prs SKILL.md, resolve-conflicts SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, and one doc-comment line in xtask/src/merge_plan.rs. No code or constants changed, so nothing was rebuilt (the fix agent's `cargo test -p xtask` 121 passed and clippy stand).
- The bump PR (`chore(process): PROCESS_VERSION <n>`) and #1488 are exempted from "must not edit PROCESS_VERSION" in all three texts, and the bump PR is described as MECHANICAL, read by the merging session, no agent review, in AGENTS.md and review-prs. The texts agree with each other.
- The MECHANICAL lists (AGENTS.md, resolve-conflicts, merge_plan.rs) keep `PROCESS_VERSION` with a matching note for branches opened before #1153.

Notes (not blocking)
- The maintainer accepted the rule itself in the question dialog on 2026-11-13, as recorded in a PR comment, so the earlier needs-maintainer question is answered.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
